original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Independently certify the exact minimum scalar ADD count for the fixed R439 frame-509 Boolean endpoint in PR #1221 and enumerate all shortest words on its four named registers.
scope_change_reason: The original H2/K helper-star route overlaps the exact dirty-target relaxation in PR #1306 and semantic-D bridge work in PR #1311. This contribution changes the object to the open PR #1221 frame-509 block. Concurrent PR #1344 independently verifies its matrices and splice but explicitly makes no minimum claim; this package supplies only that distinct local optimality statement and shortest-word classification.
bottleneck_link: This is a bit-supplier circuit result, but the selected recursive bound remains complex-limited; it provides a certified local floor for one bit-block rewrite and does not change the paid moment.
stop_rule: Stop after verifying the fixed Boolean endpoint, integer transfer difference, complete four-register CNOT census through length three, and failure controls; do not search for a full-block factorization or rerun the selected construction.
evidence: The exact endpoint changes three distinct destinations, so every scalar one-destination ADD word needs at least three operations; PR #1221's word attains three. The standard-library verifier checks all 16 Boolean inputs, the exact integer matrix difference 2 e_h e_a^T, and all 1+12+144+1728 four-register CNOT words through length three. The target has no shorter realization and exactly three length-three realizations. PR #1344's matrix and splice replay is credited but not repeated.
